title: Magnetic contacts on freestanding superconducting LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ micromembranes
authors: Thies Jansen, Pinelopi Konstantinopoulou, Niklas Martin, Fabio Miletto Granozio, Alessia Sambri, Rasmus Bjørk, Felix Trier, Thomas S. Jespersen
abstract: The superconducting two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) at the LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ (LAO-STO) interface is a promising platform for superconducting spintronics, however, integrating ferromagnetic contacts with the superconducting 2DEG remains challenging. Here, we realize superconducting LAO-STO micromembrane devices contacted by ferromagnetic nickel contacts through a side-contact geometry. Low-temperature transport measurements demonstrate that superconductivity is preserved in the presence of the ferromagnetic contacts. We show that the superconducting state is strongly influenced by the magnetic history of the nickel contacts, which generates a tunable effective magnetic field in the 2DEG. Through an effective field model, the magnetization of the contacts can be inferred from the maximum superconducting response. Our results establish ferromagnetically contacted LAO-STO as a platform for future investigations of spin injection into oxide superconductors and provide a route towards superconducting spintronic devices based on complex oxide interfaces.
summary: This work demonstrates the feasibility of using ferromagnetic contacts on superconducting LaAlO3/SrTiO3 membranes for superconducting spintronics. By measuring transport properties, the researchers showed that the superconducting state is highly sensitive to the magnetic history of the nickel contacts. This establishes a platform for studying spin injection and magnetic control in oxide superconductors.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is integrating ferromagnetic contacts with the superconducting two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) at the LaAlO3/SrTiO3 interface for superconducting spintronics.
main_result: Superconductivity is preserved in the presence of ferromagnetic contacts, and the superconducting state is strongly controlled by the magnetic history of these contacts, allowing the 2DEG to act as a sensitive magnetometer.
method: Low-temperature transport measurements, specifically measuring differential resistance (dV/dI) as a function of applied magnetic field and current bias, were used to probe the superconducting state.
model_or_system: The physical system is a superconducting 2DEG formed at the LAO-STO interface, realized in freestanding micromembranes contacted by ferromagnetic nickel. The physics is modeled using an effective field approach that accounts for the stray magnetic field generated by the contacts.
key_observables: Superconducting transition temperature, hysteretic dependence of dV/dI on magnetic field, and the switching current (Ic).
important_parameters: Low temperatures (down to 30 mK), magnetic fields (up to 6 T), and the magnetic history/magnetization state of the Ni contacts.
main_assumptions: The superconducting state is sensitive to the effective magnetic field generated by the combination of the external field and the contact magnetization.
figures_summary: Figures show SEM images of the device, resistance vs. temperature curves confirming superconductivity, and detailed dV/dI maps showing hysteretic dependence on applied magnetic fields and current bias.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the device platform, presents transport measurements demonstrating superconductivity coexistence with ferromagnetism, and then develops an effective field model to quantify how the contact magnetization dictates the superconducting response.
why_interesting: The study directly investigates the interplay between magnetism and superconductivity in complex oxide interfaces, which is a key area for understanding unconventional superconductivity and spin-charge coupling in condensed matter systems.
